name: Long Call (standard directional)
summary: Buy one OTM-to-ATM call to get leveraged upside with risk capped at the debit paid.

legs.strike_rule: 30-40 delta OTM call (first strike with delta in 0.30-0.40); if none, nearest strike above spot

max_profit: Unlimited: (underlying at exit - strike) x 100 - debit
max_loss: The debit paid x 100 per contract. Fully defined.
breakevens: strike + debit per share, at expiration only

greeks.delta: +0.30 to +0.40 per contract (+30 to +40 share equivalents)
greeks.gamma: positive, small, rises as spot approaches strike and as DTE falls
greeks.theta: negative, roughly -0.5% to -1.5% of position value per day at 45 DTE, accelerating inside 21 DTE
greeks.vega: positive, largest at ATM; a 1-point IV drop costs roughly 0.5-1.5% of the debit

when_to_use: IV rank below 35 (long premium is cheap relative to its own year), underlying above rising 20 and 50 EMA on the daily, and no earnings before the planned exit date.
entry_rules: IV rank (IVR) of the underlying < 35; skip if IVR > 50 because vega works against you
Price > 20 EMA and 20 EMA > 50 EMA on the daily chart
No earnings, no scheduled binary event before the planned exit date
Choose 30-60 DTE; never enter a directional long call with < 21 DTE unless it is an explicit 0DTE/scalp strategy
Strike by delta: 0.30-0.40. Do not pick strikes by round-number intuition
Bid/ask spread <= 10% of the mid, and open interest >= 500 on the chosen contract
Debit per contract <= 1.5% of account equity (~$750 on $50k); max 5 concurrent long-premium positions
Enter with a limit order at the mid; walk the limit up in $0.05 steps, never cross more than 25% of the spread
management_rules: Take profit at +100% of the debit (contract mid >= 2.0x entry debit)
Scale rule: at +100% you may sell half and trail the rest with a stop at entry debit (free carry)
Hard stop at -50% of the debit (contract mid <= 0.5x entry debit)
Time stop: close at 21 DTE regardless of P&L; theta decay past 21 DTE is the largest single drag on long calls
If IV rank rises above 60 while the position is up, harvest - vega gains are the first thing to reverse
Do not average down. Adding to a losing long call doubles theta exposure against the same broken thesis
exit_rules: Close (sell to close) at +100%, -50%, or 21 DTE, whichever comes first

Never hold a long call through expiration: any long call that is ITM at expiry will be auto-exercised by OCC (the $0.01 ITM rule) and deliver 100 shares you did not size for. Sell to close no later than 15:30 ET on expiration day
If the long call is OTM at 15:30 ET on expiry day and worth < $0.05, let it expire worthless rather than paying commissions and slippage
If the underlying is halted or the option goes no-bid, escalate to manual review - do not market-order out
assignment_risk: No assignment risk - you are long. The real risk is auto-EXERCISE: OCC exercises any long option $0.01 or more ITM at expiry, delivering 100 shares per contract. Automation must flatten long calls before 15:30 ET on expiration day.
buying_power: Cash debit only; no margin held beyond the premium paid.
liquidity_needs: Underlying ADV >= 2M shares; option OI >= 500 and bid/ask <= 10% of mid. Avoid names where the chain is only monthlies.
common_mistakes: Buying calls when IVR > 60 and then being right on direction but still losing to IV crush; buying 7-14 DTE for a 3-week thesis; holding to expiration and getting auto-exercised into 100 shares.
zero_dte_notes: The 30-60 DTE version is explicitly not a 0DTE strategy. See zero-dte-long-call-scalp for the 0DTE variant with its own rules.
